topic: What are the coding principles embedded in neuronal spike trains?

selected_primary_idea.title: Task- and State-Conditioned Causal Neural Code Atlas
selected_primary_idea.abstract: A staged encoding-decoding-causal framework that compares rate, timing, correlation, population geometry, and hybrid coding dimensions across held-out stimuli, states, tasks, and neurons, then gates functional claims on selective perturbation.
selected_primary_idea.research_object: Neuronal spike trains and downstream-relevant behavioral or decision outputs
selected_primary_idea.mechanism: Stimulus and task variables modulate point-process intensity, event timing, coupling, and population trajectories conditional on state.
selected_primary_idea.intervention: Matched computational nulls followed, where approved and feasible, by selective spike-pattern or population-subspace perturbation.
falsification_conditions: rate-only model matches full model across prespecified held-out conditions
timing gain disappears under count-matched jitter
correlation gain disappears under matched nulls
manifold effect is explained by nuisance variables
candidate perturbation has no selective downstream effect

rejected_ideas.title: Single universal neural code
rejected_ideas.reason: unfalsifiable across contexts and inconsistent with conditional evidence

rejected_ideas.title: Decoder-only universal criterion
rejected_ideas.reason: decodability does not establish downstream use

mcts_trace.defect: population decoder can confuse availability with use
state changes can invalidate fixed mappings
